findings.text: the Why says the three queued reviews, one of them the cited run, "recorded a brief path inside the run directory of an earlier dispatch. That dispatch had been refused at the roster cap". The cited run's own record shows the composed brief at /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20261114T121904732821-diiid-edge-current-refusal/figure-review-brief.md (dispatch-detail.json, admit_request.node.brief), and the sibling review run r-20261114T203459339663 declares its write paths and its record inside that same directory and names it, in its own manifest, "the reviewed run directory" that "no longer exists on disk", cause outside that node — no roster-cap refusal appears anywhere in the record. So the directory that vanished is the reviewed (subject) run's, which §18's Deliverable explicitly puts outside the section ("removing the reviewed run's directory is outside this section"), and the mechanism the section repairs is a different, unevidenced one.

findings.text: the first case's fallback ("If no dispatch path at the base revision records a brief that way") is the outcome the record above makes likely, and in that branch the node delivers a test that reads each request's brief as inside its own or the reviewed run's directory and "reports the section's shape as no longer reachable".
